Deviation

/dee-vee-AY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Deviation means a departure from an established course, standard, or norm.

Air traffic controllers noticed a small deviation from the flight plan and radioed the pilot to ask why the jet had drifted south of its approved route.

Worked Example

The bakery's famous sourdough had been made the same way for forty years, so when Wednesday's loaves came out darker and tangier than usual, the head baker traced the deviation to a new apprentice who had let the dough rise an extra hour.

The change in the loaves is a departure from the bakery's long-established standard recipe, which is exactly what a deviation is.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

departure: A departure is any turning away from a usual course or practice, large or small, and the word stays general. A deviation is measured against something definite — an established course, standard, or rule — so it implies a set line from which the step away can be marked.

divergence: Divergence is two paths, trends, or views pulling apart from each other, so it always involves at least two things separating. A deviation is one thing stepping away from a single established course or standard while the standard itself stays put.

irregularity: An irregularity is a flaw noticed in a record or procedure, something that fails to follow the usual rule. A deviation names the act or instance of departing from a set course or standard, and it can be deliberate, accidental, or simply measured.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

conformity: behavior that follows the accepted standard

adherence: faithful sticking to a rule or path

Where it sits · how far outside the norm it steps — variation → deviation → defiance

variation vs. deviation: A variation is a mild, often expected difference within the normal range, while a deviation is a clear departure from the established course or standard.

defiance vs. deviation: A deviation steps away from the norm, but defiance openly rejects the rule itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: off, away from

Root — via

Root — via: from Latin via, road, way

Suffix — -tion

Suffix — -tion: noun-forming ending, act or result of

Put it together

Put it together: Deviation is built from de-, 'off, away from,' the Latin root via, 'road or way,' and the noun ending -tion. A deviation is literally a step 'off the road,' a departure from the path or standard that everyone expected to be followed.

Use the root in a new word: obvious

Use the root in a new word: obvious: The answer was obvious to everyone in the room, and the word itself began as Latin obvius, 'lying in the way, right there on the road,' the same via root found in deviation.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, often technical

Deviation names the act or an instance of departing from a course, standard, or norm, and it is the noun relative of the verb deviate. It is common in technical phrases such as 'standard deviation' in statistics and 'deviation from protocol' in formal reports.
